q: Does the pentagon-over-chao ordering survive under biased (Z-dominated) noise, or does the pair-measurement hook-error structure collapse the advantage in the regime physical hardware actually operates in?
basis: The paper uses uniform circuit-level depolarizing. Real superconducting and neutral-atom platforms are strongly Z-biased. The 5-pair decomposition's ZX derivation is symmetric under Pauli frame, but bidirectional-hook-error asymmetry (Gidney's own caveat driving the low-p chao win in C3) is exactly the kind of structure that biased noise amplifies.
next_steps: Rewrite the paper's Stim circuit noise model to a biased-depolarizing channel with bias eta in {3, 10, 30, 100}. Re-run the same 12 (d,p) points and check whether pentagon still beats chao 12/12, whether the ratio pentagon/chao shifts monotonically with eta, and whether the low-p crossover point moves. Free compute: uicgpu A100 or CherryRd CPU.

q: How much of the pentagon advantage is retained when the physical two-qubit pair-measurement primitive is replaced by a realistic decomposed circuit (CNOT + ancilla + measurement + reset) under the same top-level physical error rate p?
basis: The paper charges one noise event per pair measurement. Real platforms decompose that into 2-3 CNOTs plus ancilla operations plus mid-circuit measurement plus reset, each carrying its own error. If pentagon's advantage is largely from the 5-vs-6-pair count, decomposition inflates both and the ratio may change qualitatively.
next_steps: Substitute each pair-measurement gate in the Stim circuit with a Bell-basis-measurement decomposition (H + CNOT + MZ + reset), reweighting noise so that per-CNOT error equals p / (avg gates per pair measurement). Re-run head-to-head at d=5,7 across the same p grid. Compare pentagon/chao ratios pre- and post-decomposition.

q: Can a graph neural network decoder trained on pentagon-tiling syndrome graphs beat correlated MWPM by enough to close the pentagon-vs-honeycomb gap at moderate p?
basis: The paper reports honeycomb wins overall (C4). If pentagon's disadvantage against honeycomb is partly a decoder-quality artifact rather than an intrinsic code-distance-per-qubit deficit, a stronger decoder could compress or reverse the gap. Honeycomb has a more homogeneous syndrome graph; pentagon has spatially heterogeneous check weights that ML decoders often exploit well.
next_steps: Use stim to sample 10M syndrome/error pairs per (family, d, p) triple. Train a small GNN decoder (message-passing on the detector graph) with LER as the loss surrogate. Compare inference-time LER against pymatching and against paper's correlated-MWPM numbers on the same shots. Free compute: uicgpu.

q: Does the pentagon code compose cleanly with active dynamical decoupling on idle data qubits, and if so does it recover part of the biased-noise-regime deficit from question 1?
basis: Pair-measurement schedules have long idle windows for data qubits during ancilla-side operations. DD pulses on idle qubits are known to convert coherent Z drift into stochastic errors, which MWPM handles better. The 6-time-step pentagon round is shorter than chao's 10, so DD budget differs.
next_steps: Add an idle-qubit noise channel with a tunable coherent-Z fraction to the Stim circuit. Model DD as a Pauli twirl that maps coherent-Z to depolarizing at rate p_dd. Sweep p_dd and check whether the pentagon-over-chao ratio recovers or degrades compared to the pure-depolarizing baseline.

q: For a fixed hardware topology (e.g. IBM heavy-hex, or a neutral-atom triangular grid), does the pentagon layout embed with acceptable SWAP overhead, and does the effective threshold after embedding still beat the chao layout on the same topology?
basis: The Cairo pentagonal tiling has degree-3 and degree-4 vertices. Heavy-hex is degree-3. Neutral-atom rearrangement is essentially all-to-all but with move latency. The paper's threshold assumes native pair measurements between any tile-adjacent pair; realistic embeddings add SWAPs whose noise is not in the paper's budget.
next_steps: Enumerate a minimum-SWAP embedding of the Cairo tiling onto heavy-hex (via subgraph isomorphism) and onto a neutral-atom rearrangement schedule. Add the embedding SWAPs to the Stim circuit as extra gates at rate p. Re-run head-to-head vs chao under the same embedding rule. Report threshold shift and pentagon-over-chao ratio degradation.
